increments.title: Restore the notification-side write when copying a notification as new
increments.diagnosis:
The diagnosis is correct but incomplete on one point that changes the shape of the gate decision. Copy SEMANTICS are not the same on the two sides. backend:.../notification/NotificationCopyMapper.java:33-85 deliberately RESETS logistical fields on a notification-side copy — transport (portOfEntry, arrivalDate, transporter), consignment contact address, internalReference, totalNoOfAnimals, totalNoOfPackages, species and unweanedAnimals, retaining only typeOfCommodity — each with an "intentionally omitted ... reset on copy" comment. The fulfilments-side copy retains EVERYTHING verbatim (NotificationFulfilmentsService.java:103-111 copies source.getFulfilments() wholesale), and so does the stub the current product behaviour is defined against (frontend:.../records/stub/lifecycle/create.js:41-50, structuredClone of source.fulfilment).

Consequence for the gate: under option (a) — POST /notifications/{sourceRef}/copy then PUT the fulfilments — the notification projection lands with arrival date, animal counts and contact address blanked by NotificationCopyMapper while the fulfilments the user actually sees in the journey still hold the source values. The dashboard row and the journey answers disagree until the first successful save re-projects everything from fulfilments (mutate.js:36-46). So option (a) is not a drop-in restoration of pre-retrofit ordering; it either needs the reset mapper bypassed for this path, or the product needs to rule on whether "copy as new" resets logistical fields at all. That ruling belongs in the same gate, and the investigator's proposed-changes list does not mention NotificationCopyMapper anywhere.
increments.refutation:
I tried to break this on all five fronts and could not. Every cited line is accurate.

DEFECT EXISTS. frontend:src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js:31-46 — real-mode `copy` makes exactly one fetch, POST `${notificationFulfilmentsUrl}/${journeyId}/copy`, and returns marshal() of that response. Contrast `create` at lines 11-29 which POSTs /notifications first (backend mints the ref) then PUTs the fulfilments aggregate at that same ref; the comment at lines 7-10 states the ordering as a rule. backend:.../notificationfulfilments/NotificationFulfilmentsService.java:85-128 confirms copy() mints its own ref via referenceNumberGenerator.generate() and calls only notificationFulfilmentsRepository.insert(copy) — no Notification is written. Real mode is the default (frontend:src/server/app/services/mode.js:1, `process.env.LIVE_ANIMALS_MODE ?? 'real'`) and the stack sets it explicitly (docker/stack/frontend.compose.yml:52). Not already-fixed, not cannot-reproduce.

ROOT CAUSE, NOT SYMPTOM. I looked one level down for an escape hatch and there is none. The dashboard list is purely notification-side: read.js:22-48 fetches `${notificationsUrl}?page=...` with no aggregation join, and the comment at 16-21 says so. The save path mutate.js:36-46 POSTs /notifications with `referenceNumber: journeyId` set, which backend NotificationService.java:85-92 (saveOriginOfImport) routes to updateNotification, and updateNotification at 380-384 throws NotFoundException for an unknown reference. I checked whether the retry wrapper rescues it: real/projections/put-projection.js:17-38 retries the identical body MAX_PROJECTION_ATTEMPTS times and then rethrows — there is no 404-to-create fallback, so the first save of a copy is a hard recoverable-error page. transition.js:23-83 confirms finalise/amend/cancelAmend/softDelete each dual-post to `${notificationsUrl}/${journeyId}/...`, all of which 404 for a copy. I also checked for a way to fix this purely in the frontend while keeping the idempotent call: NotificationController.java exposes only POST /notifications, POST /{ref}/copy, /submit, /amend, /cancel-amend, /soft-delete, GET, DELETE — there is NO PUT /notifications/{ref} upsert. So the frontend genuinely cannot create a Notification at a ref the fulfilments copy already minted. The needs-decision framing survives that attack.

MATCHES THE SNAG. "Copy as new is broken" — the copy vanishes from the dashboard and dies on first save. That is the reporter's complaint.

VERDICT IS RIGHT, AND FOR THE RIGHT REASON. The idempotency machinery is real and load-bearing: notification-actions/controller.js:26-42 reads a hidden idempotencyKey from the payload, and recoverCopy at 12-24 re-renders the dashboard or notification view with the SAME key preserved on a recoverable 500, so the user's retry dedupes at NotificationFulfilmentsService.java:88-95 (findCopy by idempotency key). The notification-side copy endpoint has no key. So option (a) really does trade retry-safety for the fix, and option (b) really does require a backend change. Two defensible answers in different repos = needs-decision, correctly called.

ONE SUBSTANTIVE GAP the investigator missed (see correctedDiagnosis) — copy SEMANTICS diverge between the two aggregates, which adds a third dimension to the gate decision and means option (a) is not the clean "restore pre-retrofit ordering" it is billed as.

REPO LIST is complete. frontend + tests under option (a); frontend + backend + tests under option (b). Nothing else consumes the copy path — admin reads notifications but does not copy, and the stub repo is uninvolved.

increments.gate: Which side mints the copied notification's reference number, and where does the dual write live? Option (a) notification-first, mirroring `create`: POST /notifications/{sourceRef}/copy to mint the new reference and copy the display fields, then PUT /notification-fulfilments/{newRef} with the source's fulfilments — frontend-only, consistent with the "frontend adapter owns the dual write" convention documented in real/lifecycle/transition.js:6-10, but it drops the Idempotency-Key dedupe, so a retry after a recoverable 500 mints a second copy and the retry-stability contract in notification-actions/controller.test.js:69-84 no longer holds in real mode. Option (b) backend dual write: extend NotificationFulfilmentsService.copy (or add an upsert-at-reference path to POST /notifications) so one idempotent call creates BOTH documents at one reference — preserves the Idempotency-Key retry semantics the retrofit deliberately introduced, but moves the dual write into the backend, against the convention above, and makes this a backend + frontend change. Pick (a) or (b) before implementation; the fix files differ by repo depending on the answer.
increments.notes: Real-mode "Copy as new" creates only the canonical notification-fulfilments document and never the paired Notification record at the copy's new reference. The copy therefore never appears on the dashboard (which lists from /notifications), and the first save, submit, amend or delete of the copy 404s on the notification side and surfaces the recoverable-error page. Introduced by the EUDPA-288 retrofit (23f2fdb4), which swapped the pre-retrofit POST /notifications/{ref}/copy for POST /notification-fulfilments/{id}/copy without restoring the notification-side write. Invisible to the frontend's own suites because they run in stub mode, where one in-memory map backs both reads. The defect is unambiguous; the fix shape is a design call, because the only idempotent copy endpoint is the fulfilments one and the only reference-minting endpoint the dashboard reads from is the notification one.

increments.snagText: Copy as new CSS is off
increments.title: Stop .app-link-button resetting font-family so link-buttons render in GDS Transport
increments.diagnosis:
"Copy as new" on the notification dashboard renders in the browser's default serif (Times) while every action next to it renders in GDS Transport. The cause is a single conflicting declaration in the custom stylesheet.

WHERE THE ELEMENT IS
`frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:91-106` renders each summary-card action two ways. Actions carrying an `href` render as `<a class="govuk-link">`; actions carrying a `postAction` render as `<button type="submit" class="govuk-link app-link-button">` inside a `<form class="app-form-inline">` (CSRF crumb + idempotency key must be POSTed, so it cannot be an anchor). `frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:19-24` gives the copy action a `postAction`, so on a DRAFT row "Copy as new" is the ONLY `<button>` among Resume / Delete anchors — it is visibly the odd one out, which is exactly what "CSS is off" describes. (On a SUBMITTED row "Amend" is a button too, so it is affected identically.)

ROOT CAUSE — cascade conflict on font-family
`frontend:src/client/stylesheets/core/_main.scss:16` declares `font-family: inherit` on `.app-link-button`. govuk-frontend 6.4.0 declares `font-family: GDS Transport, arial, sans-serif` on `.govuk-link, a`. Both selectors are specificity 0-1-0, so source order decides. Verified in the built bundle `frontend:.public/stylesheets/application.1ee130c.min.css`:
  - byte 941  → `.govuk-link,a{font-family:GDS Transport,arial,sans-serif;...}`
  - byte 1080 → the same rule again
  - byte 137469 → `.app-link-button{background:none;border:none;padding:0;cursor:pointer;font-size:inherit;font-family:inherit;font-weight:inherit;display:inline;vertical-align:baseline;line-height:inherit;color:var(--govuk-link-colour,#1a65a6)}`
`.app-link-button` is emitted last (application.scss `@use` order: `govuk-frontend` then `variables`/`helpers`/`core`), so `font-family: inherit` wins on the `<button>` and defeats `.govuk-link`.

WHY `inherit` RESOLVES TO SERIF
govuk-frontend 6.4.0 sets font-family per component class only — there is no global rule to inherit from. Proof: `grep -o "body{[^}]*}"` on the built bundle returns exactly `body{margin:0;background-color:var(--govuk-body-background-colour,#fff)}`, and `.govuk-template` emits only background-colour / text-size-adjust / scroll-padding / overflow. The full inventory of `font-family:GDS Transport` rules in the bundle (53 of them, captured at `~/git/defra/trade-imports-animals/workareas/shared/frontend-snagging-eudpa315/gdsfont.txt`) contains `.govuk-summary-card__title` but NOT `.govuk-summary-card`, `.govuk-summary-card__title-wrapper`, `.govuk-summary-card__actions` or `.govuk-summary-card__action`. So no ancestor of the button supplies a family, `inherit` falls through to the root initial value, and Chrome computes `Times`. A previous live check at 1440px recorded exactly this: `.app-link-button` computed `Times` while its sibling `a.govuk-link` in the same `<ul>` computed `"GDS Transport", arial, sans-serif`.

WHY THE OTHER DECLARATIONS ARE FINE — `font-size: inherit`, `font-weight: inherit` and `line-height: inherit` do NOT conflict, because `.govuk-link` sets none of them; the button correctly inherits size 19 and bold from `.govuk-summary-card__actions` (bundle byte ~229 of the summary-card mixin sets `govuk-font-size(19)` + `govuk-typography-weight-bold`). `font-family` is the only broken declaration. The explicit `color` override at `_main.scss:23` is correct and load-bearing (govuk sets link colour via `:link`, which never matches `<button>`) and must stay.

BLAST RADIUS — the same defect affects every `.app-link-button` in the app, all of which also carry `.govuk-link`: `features/commodities/consignment-details/_selected-commodities-table.njk:8`, `features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:19`, `features/documents/contracts/remove-action.js:12`. One stylesheet edit fixes all of them.

ALTERNATIVE RULED OUT — a wrapping/width theory (that the action row wraps because `frontend:src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:57` hard-codes `govuk-grid-column-two-thirds` where the pre-retrofit layout used `govuk-grid-column-full`). That width regression is real and worth its own ticket, but it is a whole-page layout change affecting every screen — it does not single out "Copy as new", and fixing it would leave the button still rendering in Times. The font-family conflict is the defect that makes this one element, and only this element, look wrong.
increments.refutation:
I attacked this on all five fronts and could not break it. It survives, and I was able to upgrade the evidence from static to live-measured.

FRONT 1 — DOES THE DEFECT EXIST? Yes, verified in source and at runtime.
`frontend:src/client/stylesheets/core/_main.scss:11-32` contains the `.app-link-button` rule, and line 17 is `font-family: inherit;` — the only `font-family` declaration in the entire app source (`grep -rn "font-family" src/client/ src/server/` returns exactly that one hit). The built bundle agrees: `grep -o "app-link-button{[^}]*}" .public/stylesheets/application.*.min.css` emits `...font-size:inherit;font-family:inherit;font-weight:inherit;...`.

I then measured it live. The stack is up on :3000, so I loaded a frontend-rendered page (`http://localhost:3000/definitely-not-a-real-page`, 404 via `shared/layout.njk`, so the real `application.css` is the only stylesheet loaded) and injected the exact DOM the dashboard emits — `.govuk-summary-card > .govuk-summary-card__title-wrapper > ul.govuk-summary-card__actions > li.govuk-summary-card__action > form.app-form-inline > button.govuk-link.app-link-button`, alongside a sibling `a.govuk-link`. Computed styles:
  button → fontFamily `Times`, fontSize 19px, fontWeight 700, lineHeight 25px, color rgb(26,101,166)
  link   → fontFamily `"GDS Transport", arial, sans-serif`, fontSize 19px, fontWeight 700, lineHeight 25px, color rgb(26,101,166)
Font-family is the ONLY divergent property, exactly as diagnosed. That also independently confirms the investigator's "the other `inherit` declarations are fine" claim rather than taking it on trust.

FRONT 2 — ROOT CAUSE OR SYMPTOM? Root cause, and the mechanism checks out one level up and one level down.
Up: I traced why `inherit` resolves to serif rather than trusting the bundle grep. `govuk-frontend@6.4.0` (`node_modules/govuk-frontend/package.json:4`) applies typography per component class only. `objects/_template.mixin.scss:45-51` gives `<body>` (`.govuk-template__body`) only `margin: 0` + `background-color` — confirmed in the bundle (`govuk-template__body{margin:0;background-color:var(--govuk-body-background-colour,#fff)}`). `core/_global-styles.mixin.scss` adds only `a { @extend %govuk-link }` and `p { @extend %govuk-body-m }` — that is where the bundle's `.govuk-link,a` selector comes from, and it does not touch `body`. `components/summary-list/_mixin.scss:229-231` gives `.govuk-summary-card__actions` `govuk-font-size(19)` + `govuk-typography-weight-bold` but NO family; `:245` gives `.govuk-summary-card__action` only `display`. So no ancestor supplies a family — and my live probe measured `getComputedStyle(document.body).fontFamily === "Times"` and `.govuk-summary-card__actions` `=== "Times"`, proving it directly rather than by absence-of-grep-hit.
Down: `.govuk-link`'s family comes from `core/_links.scss` → `_links.mixin.scss:6-11` → `helpers/_links.scss:17-18` `govuk-link-common` → `govuk-typography-common`. Both selectors are 0-1-0, and app CSS is emitted after govuk (byte ordering in gdsfont.txt: `.govuk-link,a` at 941, `.notification-list__*` at 140213), so source order decides and `inherit` wins.
I also proved the proposed fix is sufficient AND complete, live: I removed `font-family` from the `.app-link-button` CSSOM rule and re-measured. The button then computed `"GDS Transport", arial, sans-serif` / 19px / 700 / 25px / rgb(26,101,166) / underline — identical to the anchor on every typographic property. One declaration deleted, defect gone, nothing else needed. No replacement `font-family` is required.

FRONT 3 — DOES IT MATCH THE SNAG? Yes.
`workareas/shared/frontend-snagging-eudpa315/snags.txt` shows snag-001 "Copy as new is broken" (functional) and snag-002 "Copy as new CSS is off" (visual) as a pair about the same element. A bold serif sitting between two sans-serif siblings in the same `<ul>` is precisely "CSS is off". I hunted for rival visual defects and ruled each out: `.app-form-inline { display: contents }` does not disturb the flex layout; action separators/spacing are supplied by `summary-list/_mixin.scss:118-155` (margin-left/padding-left + border-left) and apply to `<li>`s regardless of their child element, so the row is not running together; and the app's markup is byte-for-byte the shape of govuk's own fixture `summary-list/template-as-a-summary-card-with-actions.html:6-10`. I also checked the investigator's ruled-out width theory is at least real — `shared/layout.njk:57` is indeed `govuk-grid-column-two-thirds` — and agree it does not single out this one element.
The "actionable vs needs-decision" challenge fails: no target design has been invented. `.app-link-button` exists solely to make a POST button look like the link next to it (introduced by `c64ec822 feat(EUDPA-172): copy as new`, the commit that created `_main.scss`), and every one of its four call sites pairs it with `govuk-link`. Matching the adjacent anchor is the class's own stated intent, found in the repo, not a taste call. The two candidate fixes (delete the declaration vs. set `$govuk-font-family`) are visually identical, so there is no behavioural fork to decide.

FRONT 4 — REPO LIST. `frontend` alone is correct; I found nothing to add.
I verified all four call sites and all four pair with `govuk-link`, so deleting the declaration cannot orphan any of them: `features/commodities/consignment-details/_selected-commodities-table.njk:8`, `features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:19`, `features/dashboard/template.njk:98`, `features/documents/contracts/remove-action.js:12`.
For `tests`: the specs that touch this element use role/name locators (`tests/e2e/pages/notification-view-states.spec.ts:33,57-58`, `page-objects/notification/notification-dashboard-page.ts:170`), which a font-family change cannot affect; text and colour are unchanged so axe outcomes are unchanged. The one real risk was the visual-regression baseline `tests/e2e/visual/origin-of-import.visual.spec.ts:12` (`toHaveScreenshot`, fullPage) — but origin-of-import is not one of the four `.app-link-button` call sites, so the baseline is untouched. `tests` therefore stays out of scope, though see ladder gap 3.
Incidental, not a fix requirement: `page-objects/notification/notification-view-page.ts:22` still looks for a "Copy as new" button on the notification view, but `grep -rni "copy as new"` across `frontend:src/server/app` shows it renders only on the dashboard now. That page object is stale — a pre-existing issue for whoever owns snag-006's a11y failures, not this ticket.

FRONT 5 — LADDER HONESTY. Mostly sound, with real gaps listed separately.
All seven scripts exist (`package.json:14,21,29,32,37`). Step 4 is a genuine gate — my measurement proves the new test goes red on unfixed code (Times vs GDS Transport). Steps 1, 3, 6 are legitimate build/lint checks. But step 2 is an inspection with no pass/fail criterion, and step 5 (vitest) cannot exercise CSS in either direction, so neither adds verification power.

ONE OBSERVATION FOR THE IMPLEMENTOR, not a defect: after the fix the button still computes `display: inline-block` while the sibling anchor computes `inline` (measured live). This is true both before and after the edit, so it is not caused by the change and does not block it — but it means the button is not layout-identical to the link, and the implementor should not chase it as a regression.

filesToTouch.what: Delete the `font-family: inherit;` declaration from the `.app-link-button` rule (line 16). Change nothing else in that rule — `background`, `border`, `padding`, `cursor`, `font-size: inherit`, `font-weight: inherit`, `display: inline`, `vertical-align: baseline`, `line-height: inherit`, the `color` declaration and the `:hover` / `:active` blocks all stay exactly as they are, as does the existing comment above `color`. The container here is doubly narrowed: `shared/layout.njk:57` wraps all page content in `govuk-grid-column-two-thirds`, and `template.njk:11-12`/`23` then splits that again into two `govuk-grid-column-one-half` columns. It cites AUTOCOMPLETE-ASSESSMENT.md (not present in any repo or workarea — I searched) and "Sam's ruling". The prototype work it reverted is commits 7edced0d (inc-058, country-of-origin canary) and b79c1379 (inc-059, port-of-entry rollout).

2. Current state confirmed by reading the code, not inferred:
- `grep -rn "data-select-autocomplete\|selectAutocomplete" src webpack.config.js` returns nothing. `webpack.config.js:22-30` has only `application` and `documents` entries; `src/client/javascripts/` contains only `application.js`. `accessible-autocomplete` is absent from `package.json`.

- frontend:.../features/origin/template.njk:15, .../destination-country/template.njk:13, .../port-of-exit/template.njk:13 and .../addresses/create-address/create-address.njk:68 are the same pattern over the 31-country fixtures (`countries-origin.json`, `countries.json`), i.e. 33 options each.

- frontend:.../commodities/search/search.njk is still named and keyed "search" (copy.en.js:4 `search:`) but contains no search box at all — just grouped checkboxes (search.njk:19-29). That build mounts the journey under a set prefix — confirmed inside the container and on the branch: trade-imports-animals-frontend `spike/trace-to-requirements`:src/server/router.js:9 `export const DEFAULT_SET_BASE = '/live-animals'` and :23 `routes: { prefix: '/live-animals' }`. increments.refutation:
I tried hard to break this and could not. Every load-bearing fact re-verified, and the one genuinely unproven claim I found I then proved FOR the investigator by experiment.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY
1. The mechanism. `docker ps` confirms the stack serves `defradigital/trade-imports-animals-frontend:spike-trace-to-requirements`, and `docker exec ... ls /home/node/src/server/app/sets` returns `live-animals` + `plant-products` — it is the two-set prefixed build. The local checkout is main-lineage: frontend `fix/EUDPA-320-fix-link-button-font-family`, and frontend:src/server/router.js:7,20 registers `liveAnimals` from `./app/routes.js` with NO prefix, and frontend:src/server/app/sets/ contains only `live-animals`. So local source and running container are different applications, exactly as claimed.
2. The break point. tests:page-objects/base/base-page.ts:81 `return \`/notifications/${journeyId}${suffix}\`` and :85 `pathname.match(/^\/notifications\/([^/]+)/)` are set-prefix-blind, throwing at :87. `tim workspace status --json` puts tests on `fix/EUDPA-319-hub-commodity-totals-boxes` (main lineage).
3. Not a11y-specific. tests:playwright.docker-compose.config.ts:8-9 pins `e2e: 'http://localhost:3000'` — the suite has no stack of its own, it runs against whatever the shared workspace stack is serving. The pre-existing control log logs/snag-006-refute-e2e-import-type.log shows `tests/e2e/features/import-type-routing.spec.ts` dying with the identical `No journey id in notification URL: http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-KMW1G5/import-type` at base-page.ts:87. Confirmed.

THE HOLE I FOUND, AND CLOSED
The diagnosis's headline claim — "it is NOT an accessibility defect" — was asserted, not evidenced. All four failures die BEFORE any scan (three at base-page.ts:87, one at notification-view-page.ts:47 then `No accessibility scans were run` at fixtures/a11y.ts:78). "axe never ran" is not the same as "axe would find nothing", so those pages could still have carried real WCAG violations and the ladder's step 7 "expect 12 passed, 0 failed" was a guess.

I settled it. I cut a git worktree of tests `spike/trace-to-requirements` (the branch whose page objects match the running image), symlinked node_modules, and ran all six live-animals a11y specs against the untouched running stack — no reseed, no stack rebuild, siblings undisturbed. Logs: workareas/shared/frontend-snagging-eudpa315/logs/snag-006-refute-a11y-spike.log and snag-006-refute-a11y-view.log. Result: 6 of 6 green (3 journey-state specs 45.3s; view-states + dashboard-views + 1 pre-existing skip 7.3s). Zero axe violations on the pages that had never been scanned. So the investigator's conclusion is now proven rather than inferred — there is no accessibility defect anywhere in the live-animals suite, on the very build Sam is looking at.

WHY needs-decision SURVIVES, AND IS ACTUALLY FIRMER THAN THE INVESTIGATOR ARGUED
My run collapses one arm of the gate to zero work: against the prefixed build, the matching tests branch is already 100% green, so if "the prefixed build" is the target there is no snag fix at all — only a workspace alignment (`tim workspace branch`), not a 66-file port. The other arm (rebuild the stack from local repos/ so the un-prefixed main build is served) is still untested by anyone, and testing it means rebuilding a stack five sibling agents are mid-run against. Which world EUDPA-315 is snagging is a human call about programme sequencing, and it swings the outcome between "no code" and "back-port set-base awareness onto main-lineage tests". That is a decision, not an implementable fix. `actionable` would be wrong.

A CONCRETE FLAW IN THE PROPOSED CHANGE (not enough to break the verdict, but the implementor must not copy it verbatim)
The proposed guard `tests:tests/e2e/features/route-base-parity.spec.ts` would not fire in the lane the snag names. package.json:28 defines `test:docker-compose:a11y` as `--grep '@a11y'`, and e2e feature specs carry no such tag (verified: `grep -n "@a11y" tests/e2e/features/reference-strip.spec.ts` returns nothing). Ladder step 4 invokes the guard by explicit path so it appears to work, but the real invocation in step 7 would silently skip it and the a11y lane would still emit its wall of identical `No journey id` failures. The guard must be tagged so it runs in BOTH lanes (or live in a global setup / the a11y fixture), otherwise it solves the problem only for the lane that was never the complaint.

The `tests` repo list is correct — my run rules the frontend out as a source of a11y defect, so no frontend change is implied.
